messages:
Anna_Sales: Quick heads-up — CobaltHealth wants a short POC focused on latency + sustained throughput for conversational generation + embeddings. They asked for a 15min sustained run at 200 qps with 3 microbursts to 1k qps. Also need cost estimate and an ops playbook. Can SEs own coordination?
Devon_SE: I can lead. Proposed load plan: warmup 5m @50qps, ramp 5m ->200qps, sustain 15m, then 3x microbursts (1k qps for 30s) spaced ~3m. Workload mix: 70% gen (avg 50 tokens, max 256), 30% embeddings/rerank. We'll baseline on redwood/seq-2 and a quantized variant for cost.
Liam_SRE: Ops checklist for Dedicated: reserve 2x 8-GPU pools for baseline, autoscale policy for bursts, pre-load KV cache with top prefixes, set node drain timeout to 90s. Configure request timeout to 30s. Add their egress IPs to firewall allowlist and provision test client certs.
Sasha_Eng: If bursts cause tail issues, enable fallback to seq-2-small for <=50ms penalty but much lower GPU utilization. Also recommend enabling prefix/KV caching + request-level batching cap 64. For quantized runs, we should do a quick quality smoke to verify generation fidelity before pricing.
Jordan_SE: Pricing ask from them: what's ballpark token/unit cost for a POC like this (sustained + burst)? Can we provide a short quote comparing hosted vs Dedicated commit?
Devon_SE: Rough back-of-envelope: assume avg gen 50 tokens per request, 200 qps sustained -> 10k tokens/sec -> 36M tokens/hr. If hosted unit ~ $0.00012/token (example) -> ~ $4.3k/hr (sustained). Bursts add marginal compute; Dedicated commit brings that down significantly. I'll produce a cleaned estimate after we run a 30m sweep.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Dedicated pool reservation request submitted (req-4523) — ETA 18:30 UTC.
Anna_Sales: Can we target a run tomorrow 16:00 PT? They need results for procurement briefing.
Liam_SRE: Tomorrow 16:00 PT works if pools are reserved and we have client IPs + certs. I will do prewarm + KV preload 30m prior. Who has contact at Cobalt?
Anna_Sales: Contact is Maya Sharma (maya@cobalthealth). I'll share IPs + SCQ when I get them.
Devon_SE: Load test tooling: vegeta for embeddings/rerank, and our streaming harness for gen. Sample commands:
```
# embeddings qps via vegeta
vegeta attack -rate=200 -duration=900s -targets=emb_targets.txt | vegeta report -type=json > embed_report.json
# streaming generation harness
python tools/run_stream_bench.py --qps 200 --model redwood/seq-2 --concurrency 40 --duration 900
```
Sasha_Eng: Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency (token-level for stream), 429s, OOMs, GPU util, GPU mem, host CPU, socket latency to KMS, and trace ids for any failures. Add model-level traces so we can correlate KV cache hits.
Jordan_SE: They also asked about KMS/HSM latency impact and whether envelope key operations add notable per-request latency. Need verification.
Devon_SE: We measured KMS envelope sign ~2-3ms in our infra with regional KMS. We'll include a test run with KMS enabled so they see the number in their environment.
Liam_SRE: Quick runbook for POC day (high-level):
1) Reserve pools + confirm certs/IPs.
2) Deploy canary model variant to both pools.
3) Prewarm: push ~10k warm requests across prefixes, preload KV cache.
4) Run ramp/warmup then sustained run per plan.
5) Execute 3 microbursts.
6) Repeat baseline once more.
7) Collect traces, GPU profiles, and token-level latency.
8) Compile results + cost calc + suggested rollout (fallbacks, quantization).
I'll attach this checklist to the POC ticket.
Devon_SE: For the initial sweep I'll run: baseline (seq-2), fallback enabled run, and quantized run (int8/4 where safe). Each run ~20-30min.
Sasha_Eng: Security questionnaire: I'll own runtime key mgmt, audit logs, and HSM/KMS answers. Will draft short answers + sample audit snapshot.
Anna_Sales: Perfect. Action items: Devon -> run initial sweep and post numbers by EOD; Liam -> confirm pool reservation + prewarm timeline; Sasha -> start SCQ draft; Jordan -> prepare hosted vs Dedicated price bullets.
Jordan_SE: Will do. Expect a short quote doc by EOD.
Anna_Sales: Thanks team — please ping here when you have concrete numbers. :thumbsup:
